title: Conjecture (Section 7)
statement_text: For any integer $d\geq 1$ and positive integers $N_1,\dots,N_d$, with $N=(N_1,\dots,N_d)$, $$\mathrm{disc}(\mathcal{A}_N) = \Theta_d\!\left(\max_{I \subseteq [d]} \left(\prod_{i \in I} N_i\right)^{\frac{1}{2|I|+2}}\right),$$ that is, the known lower bound for the discrepancy of arithmetic progressions in the grid $[N_1]\times\cdots\times[N_d]$ is tight up to a constant factor depending only on $d$.
context_text: For a finite set $\Omega$ and a family $\mathcal{A}$ of subsets, a colouring is a map $\chi:\Omega\to\{1,-1\}$. With $\chi(A)=\sum_{x\in A}\chi(x)$, the discrepancy is $\mathrm{disc}(\mathcal{A})=\min_\chi\max_{A\in\mathcal{A}}|\chi(A)|$. An arithmetic progression in $d$ dimensions is a set $\{a+ib : i=0,\dots,l-1\}$ with $a,b\in\mathbb{Z}^d$, $b\neq0$, $l\in\mathbb{N}$. $\mathcal{A}_N$ is the family of such progressions contained in the grid $[N_1]\times\cdots\times[N_d]$, where $N=(N_1,\dots,N_d)$, and $\prod_{i\in\emptyset}N_i=1$. In dimension 1, Roth's lower bound $cN^{1/4}$ and the Matoušek–Spencer upper bound determine the discrepancy up to a constant. Valkó proved $N^{d/(2d+2)}$ up to a $(\log N)^{5/2}$ factor for the cube $[N]^d$. The authors show $\mathrm{disc}=\Theta_d(N^{d/(2d+2)})$ for cubes, and $\Theta_d((N_1\cdots N_d)^{1/(2d+2)})$ for grids with comparable sides. For general grids with $N_1\cdots N_d\ge3$ they prove $c_d M\le\mathrm{disc}(\mathcal{A}_N)\le C_d\frac{\log(N_1\cdots N_d)}{\log\log(N_1\cdots N_d)}M$, where $M=\max_{I\subseteq[d]}(\prod_{i\in I}N_i)^{1/(2|I|+2)}$. The bounds differ by more than a constant in some regimes even for $d=2$, e.g. $N=(N,\sqrt N(\log N)^k)$. The conjecture is that the lower bound is tight, i.e. the sub-logarithmic factor can be removed. This is discrepancy theory rather than graph theory.
notes: Section 7 is not reproduced in the PDF extraction; the conjecture is described by reference in the paper's organization paragraph. The statement above is reconstructed from Theorem 1.3 and the prose description 'a conjecture that the lower bound for the discrepancy for grids in Theorem 1.3 is tight up to the constant factor'.
paper_title: Discrepancy of arithmetic progressions in grids
